Both ask the pointwise-dominance/maxima lemma, not the original equal-maxima/meeting theorem. The lemma is true: evaluate f at a maximizer ofg. Premises differ: f=g=0 meets the original equal-maxima premise but not strict dominance, while f=1,g=0 meets the copied premise but not equal maxima. Retain any generic rubric credit separately; this is not original recovery.

For a>0, the proposed parabola and line intersect at0 andsqrt(3)/a. Their area is sqrt(3)/(2a^2), unbounded as a→0+, and their separation is not the displayed sqrt(4-a^2)/sqrt(3). At a=1 the area already exceeds1/2. The curves and task differ from the fixed-cubic source.

Seed0 leaves the integrand unspecified. The families gamma/(1+(x/a)^n), with gamma=1 or1/2, obey the qualitative bounds/threshold but have limits gamma*a. For n>1 the tail is at most gamma*a/(n-1); on[0,(1-epsilon)a] the integrand is at least gamma/(1+(1-epsilon)^n), proving the limit by squeezing. Seed1 uses f(x/a^n): taking f(u)=exp(-u) gives integral a^n, divergent at a=2, not2. Neither recovers the specified source integrand.

Seed0 omits an extremal target: both-1011 and-1034 satisfy its conditions, so they do not determine a unique integer. Seed1 explicitly asks for the smallest, whose value is-9981, not-1011. The original asks for the largest. These are different task specifications even though the supplied answer satisfies the shared congruence.

Without a fixed set size there is no finite maximum number of sets. For any N>=3, let S_i be the set of edges incident to vertexi in the complete graph K_N. Any two sets share exactly their connecting edge, no edge is common to all sets, and each d_x=1<=44. All displayed counting observations can hold with arbitrarily largeN. The source instead fixes1987 sets of size45 and asks for union size.
